content.title: Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf’s Pay Rises to $40 Million in Watershed Year for Bank
content.summary: Wells Fargo paid Chief Executive Charlie Scharf $40 million for 2025, a 28% raise from a year earlier.  Scharf earned a base salary of $2.5 million and a cash bonus of $9.4 million, according to a securities filing Thursday.  Over the summer, it was freed from a Federal Reserve punishment that had handcuffed growth at the bank since its fake-accounts scandal erupted around a decade ago.

content.title: Copper Prices Top $14,500 a Ton For First Time

content.title: Wells Fargo’s FiNet Recruits Financial Advisors From Ameriprise, Raymond James, UBS
content.summary: Wells Fargo  has scored a passel of recruiting wins this year as it seeks to draw advisors to FiNet, its independent wealth management channel.  The largest practice, Houser, Plessl & Staples Wealth Management, based in Allentown, Pa., has joined FiNet from  Ameriprise  where the team managed more than $530 million in client assets.  The same day, advisor Paolo Thompson joined Merritt Point Advisors, a FiNet practice, from Raymond James, where he managed more than $400 million in assets.
